werk/sarah-mclachlan-solace.text:
Solace is Sarah McLachlan's second studio album. It was released on Nettwerk in Canada in June 1991 and on Arista in the United States in January 1992. It was the first of many albums that Pierre Marchand produced for her. It made her a star in Canada, with the hits The Path of Thorns (Terms) and Into the Fire, and went double platinum for sales of 200,000 copies.

Outside Canada the breakthrough only came with the next album, Fumbling Towards Ecstasy, although the reviews were favourable internationally too. The Los Angeles Times heard in the songs a lovely echo of Joni Mitchell, Judy Collins and Sandy Denny, without it ever becoming imitation, and praised the atmospheric production. The Chicago Tribune felt that, because of the sombre tone, no single track really stood out. The Rolling Stone Album Guide called it a considerable leap in maturity and focus in 2004.
werk/sarah-mclachlan-solace.listen: Listen to The Path of Thorns, one of the two hit singles, and notice how her voice carries the song.

werk/scorpions-fly-to-the-rainbow.text:
After the tour for Lonesome Crow, as the support act for UFO, guitarist Michael Schenker was asked to join that band. His departure temporarily meant the end of Scorpions. Rudolf Schenker and Klaus Meine joined the band Dawn Road, and so a new line-up came about, with guitarist Uli Jon Roth, drummer Jürgen Rosenthal, keyboardist Achim Kirschning and bassist Francis Buchholz. That group recorded Fly to the Rainbow, which came out on RCA Records on 1 November 1974. Three songs were co-written by Michael Schenker, as part of the arrangement made when he left.

Roth plays lead and slide guitar and sings Drifting Sun, while Kirschning contributes organ, Mellotron and synthesizers. Speedy's Coming and the title song later appear on the 1978 live album Tokyo Tapes. Roth thought the cover downright ridiculous, and Metal Hammer put it on a list of the ugliest album covers.
werk/scorpions-fly-to-the-rainbow.listen: Listen to Drifting Sun and notice who is singing: guitarist Uli Jon Roth takes the lead vocal himself here.

werk/scorpions-in-trance.text:
In Trance is the third studio album by Scorpions and was released on RCA Records in 1975. It is a break with the progressive rock of the two albums before it. The songs are shorter and tighter, and long suites such as Lonesome Crow and Fly to the Rainbow are missing altogether. This produced the hard rock sound with which the band would later find worldwide success. Drummer Rudy Lenners plays on it for the first time, and the album was the first collaboration with producer Dieter Dierks.

The look changed too: for the first time the band name appears in the lettering that returns on almost all later covers. The original cover was censored, and later editions were given a covered-up image. The white Stratocaster on the cover belonged to guitarist Uli Jon Roth, who used it on all the following albums. He names In Trance, together with Virgin Killer, as his favourite album by the band.
werk/scorpions-in-trance.listen: Listen to the guitars on In Trance and notice how tight this hard rock song sounds next to the long suites of the first albums.

werk/scorpions-lonesome-crow.text:
Lonesome Crow is the debut album of the German rock band Scorpions. The group had only just turned professional and recorded the album under producer Conny Plank, reportedly in just six or seven days. It was released on 9 February 1972 in West Germany as the soundtrack to the anti-drug film Das Kalte Paradies. The style is dark and melodic, unlike the group's later work. It is also the only album with Michael Schenker as permanent lead guitarist, then only sixteen years old. He left soon afterwards for UFO.

A band member described In Search of the Peace of Mind as a ballad, the title song as a psychedelic rocker and I'm Goin' Mad as a great rocker with fine solos by Schenker. Action and I'm Goin' Mad are re-recordings of songs from an unreleased single from 1970, and thus the earliest released recordings by the band.
werk/scorpions-lonesome-crow.listen: Listen to In Search of the Peace of Mind, the album's ballad, and compare its mood with the hard-driving rocker I'm Goin' Mad.

werk/scorpions-virgin-killer.text:
Virgin Killer is the fourth studio album by Scorpions and was released on RCA Records on 22 November 1976. It was the first album by the band to attract attention outside Europe. The title refers to the time of a killer of innocence. The title song came about when guitarist Uli Jon Roth spontaneously played a riff in the rehearsal room and improvised the words virgin killer over it, a joke about Paul Stanley of Kiss, with whom the band had just toured. Klaus Meine felt he had to do something with it, and Roth wrote lyrics around it.

Musically it was a further step from psychedelic music towards hard rock. In the United States it received little attention, while in Japan it became popular. AllMusic calls it the first of four studio albums that truly defined the band, with Pictured Life and the title song as highlights. The original cover caused an outcry and was replaced in some countries.
werk/scorpions-virgin-killer.listen: Listen to Pictured Life for the hard rock sound with which the band broke away from psychedelic music.

werk/scott-joplin-maple-leaf-rag.text: On 10 August 1899, the Black pianist Scott Joplin signed a contract in Sedalia with the publisher John Stark for his Maple Leaf Rag. Ragtime is piano music with a displaced, hopping rhythm. Joplin did not receive a one-off fee, but one cent for every copy sold: royalties. That was highly unusual for a Black composer at the time. The sheet music sold well for years and made ragtime popular all over America.
werk/scott-joplin-maple-leaf-rag.listen: Hear how the left hand stays firmly on the beat, while the right hand keeps jumping just off it. That displaced rhythm is called syncopation.

werk/seal-human-being.text:
Human Being is Seal's third studio album and was released in 1998. Trevor Horn produced it. Seal wrote the title song about the murdered rappers Tupac Shakur and the Notorious B.I.G. The cover photograph is by the French fashion photographer Jean-Baptiste Mondino.

Reactions varied. Some critics found the record too dark and gloomy, others called it pure pop perfection. A remix of Lost My Faith played over the end credits of the film Entrapment in 1999. In the music video for the single, Seal appears in footage from the film, alongside Sean Connery and Catherine Zeta-Jones. Many guest musicians worked on the album, among them William Orbit, Wendy Melvoin and Lisa Coleman, and there were arrangers for the strings.
werk/seal-human-being.listen: Listen to the tone of Human Beings, which Seal wrote about two murdered rappers, and notice how dark the atmosphere is.

werk/seal-seal-iv.text:
Seal IV follows the abandoned sessions for Togetherland. The singer scrapped that album because, in his view, it was not up to the standard of his earlier work, and started again. In England the new record entered at number four. In the United States it debuted at number three on the Billboard 200, his highest position until then.

He was executive producer himself and wrote the liner notes. Many musicians contributed: Jamie Muhoberac plays keyboards on all twelve tracks, Trevor Horn plays piano, guitar and bass on a few tracks, and Nick Ingman wrote arrangements for strings and choir.
werk/seal-seal-iv.listen: Listen to Love's Divine and notice the strings and choir that Nick Ingman arranged for this song.

werk/seal-system.text:
System is the fifth album by the British soul and R&B singer Seal and was released on 12 November 2007. On his online blog he called it a return to his dance roots and his best record since his debut. Stuart Price produced the album and also recorded and mixed most of the tracks.

Bill Bottrell plays Mellotron on Just Like Before, and Heidi Klum sings along on the duet Wedding Day. In the United States it became his lowest-selling album: in its first year it sold 155,000 copies, according to Nielsen SoundScan.
werk/seal-system.listen: Listen to Wedding Day and notice how Heidi Klum's voice relates to the singer's in this duet.

werk/sex-pistols-anarchy-in-the-u-k.text: On 26 November 1976 Anarchy in the U.K., the first single by the Sex Pistols, was released. Manager Malcolm McLaren had brought singer Johnny Rotten into the band. On 1 December the band swore at the presenter Bill Grundy live on television. The next day it was on all the front pages. Concerts were cancelled and the record company dropped the band. Punk was now a scandal throughout England.
werk/sex-pistols-anarchy-in-the-u-k.listen: Hear the wall of double-tracked guitars and the sneering, half-sung, half-shouted voice of Johnny Rotten.

werk/sex-pistols-never-mind-the-bollocks.text:
By the time this only studio album by the Sex Pistols came out, the band had already caused a great deal of uproar: swearing on live television, two record companies dropping them and performances banned in parts of Britain. During the recording sessions in 1977, bassist Glen Matlock left; he plays on only one track. Sid Vicious took his place, but guitarist Steve Jones played bass on most of the songs. The producers were Chris Thomas and Bill Price.

The record was released on 28 October 1977 on Virgin Records. Shops refused to sell it and some charts left the title blank, but the album went straight to number one in England. It is often named as the most influential punk record. The raw energy and the sneering, half-sung delivery of Johnny Rotten changed popular music.
werk/sex-pistols-never-mind-the-bollocks.listen: Listen to Johnny Rotten's vocals in Anarchy In the U.K. What makes his delivery so different from ordinary singing?

werk/sex-pistols-the-great-rock-n-roll-s.text:
This double album was released on 23 February 1979 on Virgin Records as the soundtrack to the film of the same name. The band had split up a year earlier and singer Johnny Rotten did not want to take part. Manager Malcolm McLaren therefore had to sell a double LP without the original singer. He found a rehearsal session from October 1976 that producer Dave Goodman had secretly recorded. McLaren combined Lydon's vocals and Glen Matlock's bass part with newly recorded guitar and drums by Steve Jones and Paul Cook. This made it seem as if the original line-up still existed.

Many songs have no vocals by Rotten. Sid Vicious sings covers, including My Way, Jones and Cook take care of their own songs, and Edward Tudor-Pole sings the title song. There are also curiosities, such as French street musicians playing Anarchy in the UK. McLaren used the confusion to promote both the soundtrack and the film.
werk/sex-pistols-the-great-rock-n-roll-s.listen: Listen to My Way and notice how Sid Vicious sings a familiar song as a biting parody.

werk/shirley-bassey-i-ve-got-a-song-for-.text:
In 1966 Shirley Bassey left EMI's Columbia label and signed with United Artists. She stayed there for about fourteen years, until, ironically, the label was sold to EMI. I've Got a Song for You was her first record for that label. The producer was Kenneth Hume, whom she had divorced in 1965 but who remained her manager.

The album contains well-known songs from the American repertoire, including numbers by Irving Berlin, Rodgers and Hammerstein and Rodgers and Hart. It also features The Shadow of Your Smile and Strangers in the Night, as well as a new version of Kiss Me Honey Honey, which had been released as a single in 1958. In Britain the record entered at number 26, but stayed on the chart for only one week. In the United States it was released under the title Shirley Means Bassey, with a different cover.
werk/shirley-bassey-i-ve-got-a-song-for-.listen: Listen to Kiss Me Honey Honey. This is a new recording of a song that had already come out as a single in 1958, so notice how her voice sounds here.

werk/shirley-bassey-let-s-face-the-music.text:
Let's Face the Music is Shirley Bassey's sixth studio album, from 1962, with arrangements by Nelson Riddle. The record came about during a tour that Riddle made with her. Her husband and manager Kenneth Hume wrote in the sleeve notes that they were great fans of Riddle and at first thought that a joint record was impossible, because he was under contract to Capitol. Producer Norman Newell arranged his participation. During the tour the singer, the arranger and the musical director Raymond Long discussed what form the album should take. The recording sessions began shortly afterwards.

In the United States the record was released with a slightly different track list as Shirley Bassey Sings The Hit Song From Oliver!. In Britain it entered the chart in December 1962 and reached number 12. In 1971 it was reissued as What Now My Love and then reached number 17.
werk/shirley-bassey-let-s-face-the-music.listen: Listen to Let's Face the Music and Dance, a song by Irving Berlin, and notice how her voice relates to Nelson Riddle's orchestra.

werk/shirley-collins-folk-roots-new-rout.text:
Folk Roots, New Routes is a collaboration between Shirley Collins and guitarist Davy Graham, released by Decca in 1964. Ray Horricks produced the record and Gus Dudgeon recorded it. Collins sings, Graham plays guitar. According to Bob Stanley, the duo drew inspiration from North African scales, modal music and Miles Davis. It was the first time that many of these English folk songs were recorded with guitar accompaniment.

The record is regarded as a milestone of the folk revival. An NPR reviewer called it an uncompromising work that brought innovation in the midst of that revival. It set the pattern for the folk rock that followed and, decades later, inspired psych folk. Fairport Convention's Liege and Lief from 1969 is seen as a continuation of this model.
werk/shirley-collins-folk-roots-new-rout.listen: Listen to Reynardine and notice how the guitar accompanies the voice and how that sounds different from a traditional folk song.

werk/shocking-blue-at-home.text:
At Home is the second studio album by the Dutch band Shocking Blue and was released in 1969 on the Pink Elephant label. It is the first album with singer Mariska Veres. Robbie van Leeuwen brought her in from another band in order to follow the Jefferson Airplane model of a female lead singer. With her strong voice and presence, the group finally had a frontwoman who fitted. 

The record mixes influences from pop, rock and psychedelia. Songs such as California Here I Come and Harley Davidson already show an early interest in Americana. The hit Venus was missing from the original Dutch pressing and was added on international versions as the opening or closing track of side one. The song Love Buzz later became famous through a cover by the grunge band Nirvana. Acka Raga, a song by John Mayer, later became the theme tune of the BBC quiz programme Ask the Family.
werk/shocking-blue-at-home.listen: Listen to Love Buzz and notice the vocals of Mariska Veres. This is what the song sounds like that Nirvana would later cover.

werk/shocking-blue-scorpio-s-dance.text:
Scorpio's Dance is the third album by Shocking Blue, released in 1970 on Pink Elephant Records. In Japan it was released under the title Sally Was a Good Old Girl. The group continues its exploration of country and Americana, with songs such as Alaska Country and Sally Was a Good Old Girl.

At the same time the record stays true to the group's rock roots. The band grew musically, but in America the album did not do so well. Since the reissue in 1990, the singles Send Me a Postcard, Mighty Joe and Hello Darkness have appeared as bonus tracks on CD and LP. The line-up consists of singer Mariska Veres, guitarist and sitar player Robbie van Leeuwen, drummer Cor van der Beek and bassist Klaasje van der Wal.
werk/shocking-blue-scorpio-s-dance.listen: Listen to Alaska Country and notice how the influence of country comes through within the rock sound.

werk/shocking-blue-venus.text: On 7 February 1970 Venus by the Hague band Shocking Blue was at number one in America, the first Dutch number one there. Guitarist Robbie van Leeuwen wrote it, and Mariska Veres sang. But what is Dutch about Venus? Not the language, nor the style: only the musicians and the city. To an American listener it was simply a pop song. That question runs through the whole history of Nederpop.
werk/shocking-blue-venus.listen: Hear the guitar riff at the start and the low voice of Mariska Veres, which sounds a little like English with an accent.

werk/simon-en-garfunkel-bookends.text:
After the successful albums Sounds of Silence and Parsley, Sage, Rosemary and Thyme, Paul Simon suffered from writer's block. Columbia therefore had the young producer John Simon, no relation, help get the recording sessions going. The album came about in fits and starts over more than a year. The two asked for strings, brass players and percussionists, and worked for hours on a single song.

Bookends is a concept album about a human life, from childhood to old age. The first side follows the stages of life, with Save the Life of My Child, America, Old Friends and the two parts of Bookends Theme as a frame. The second side mainly contains previously released singles and songs that were intended for the film The Graduate, including Mrs. Robinson. That became a number 1 in the United States. In the United Kingdom the album reached number one, and it is regarded as a breakthrough for the duo.
werk/simon-en-garfunkel-bookends.listen: Listen to Mrs. Robinson and notice how voice and guitar carry the song, and how lively it sounds.

werk/simon-en-garfunkel-bridge-over-trou.text:
After the soundtrack for The Graduate and the successful Bookends, Art Garfunkel took a part in the film Catch-22. Filming lasted about eight months, and the partnership came under strain. Paul Simon meanwhile wrote the songs. With producer Roy Halee, the duo sought a new sound, away from ordinary folk rock, with influences from rock, gospel, jazz and world music. For the first time the accompanying session musicians were given credit, among them Hal Blaine, Joe Osborn and Larry Knechtel.

Simon wanted a gospel piano sound for the title song and brought in Knechtel for it. Garfunkel thought the song was too short, after which a third verse was added. The Boxer is also among the best-known songs. The first reviews were mixed, but later the album was praised. It won six Grammys, including Album of the Year. Shortly afterwards the two split up.
werk/simon-en-garfunkel-bridge-over-trou.listen: Listen to Bridge Over Troubled Water and notice how the song builds: the piano starts softly, and in the last verse drums and brass join in.

werk/simon-en-garfunkel-parsley-sage-ros.text:
After the success of The Sound of Silence, Columbia quickly released a second album, which the duo themselves regarded as a rush job. For this third album, Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel were given much more time: almost three months in the studio, with Bob Johnston as producer. For the first time they worked on an eight-track recorder, and Simon demanded complete control over the recordings.

The album consists largely of acoustic songs, often written during Simon's stay in England in 1965. The mood varies greatly from song to song. Scarborough Fair / Canticle combines guitar, bells and harpsichord with vocals. In 7 O'Clock News / Silent Night the two sing the Christmas carol while news reports about, among other things, the war in Vietnam can be heard over it. Critics see the album as a breakthrough in recording technique and as one of their best works. In 1999 it entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/simon-en-garfunkel-parsley-sage-ros.listen: Listen to 7 O'Clock News / Silent Night for the contrast between the soft two-part singing and the news reports cutting right through it.

werk/simon-en-garfunkel-sounds-of-silenc.text:
Sounds of Silence was released on 17 January 1966 as the second album by Simon & Garfunkel. The record owes its existence to a surprise. The opening track The Sound of Silence had already appeared in an acoustic version on Wednesday Morning, 3 A.M. Without Paul Simon or Art Garfunkel knowing, Columbia producer Tom Wilson had electric guitars, bass and drums laid under the recording in 1965. That new version came out as a single in September 1965 and then opened the album.

Simon wrote many of the songs in 1965 during his stay in London, and he already knew a number of them from his solo album The Paul Simon Songbook. Richard Cory is based on a poem by Edwin Arlington Robinson, Anji is an adaptation of an instrumental piece by guitarist Davey Graham, and Blessed was Simon's only truly new song. In 2013 the album was selected for the Library of Congress's National Recording Registry, as culturally, historically or aesthetically significant.
werk/simon-en-garfunkel-sounds-of-silenc.listen: Listen to the opening track The Sound of Silence and notice how the electric band, added to the recording afterwards, sits underneath the two voices.

werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-join-hand.text:
Join Hands is the second album by Siouxsie and the Banshees. It was released on 7 September 1979 on Polydor and reached number 13 on the British album chart. After half a year of writing, the group recorded it in May at AIR Studios in London. The subject is the First World War: Poppy Day opens with church bells and is based on the poem In Flanders Fields by John McCrae. The sound is darker and more oppressive than on the debut The Scream.

The recording sessions were tense. Guitarist John McKay and drummer Kenny Morris withdrew and quit on the day of the release, a few hours before a concert in Aberdeen. The British press was full of praise. Playground Twist, about the cruelty of children, was the only single and reached the top 30. The album closes with The Lord's Prayer, recorded in a single take.
werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-join-hand.listen: Listen to Poppy Day and notice the church bells it begins with and the long build-up to the tight, military beat of the drums.

werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-kaleidosc.text:
Kaleidoscope is the third album by Siouxsie and the Banshees and was released on 1 August 1980 on Polydor. After the departure of John McKay and Kenny Morris, guitarist John McGeoch and drummer Budgie joined the group, and the direction changed. For the first time the band used synthesizers and drum machines, especially on Red Light and Lunar Camel. Desert Kisses is almost a ballad. The recording sessions ran from January to May 1980.

The singles Happy House and Christine preceded it. The album reached number 5 on the British chart, the highest the group achieved. Melody Maker called it a kaleidoscope of sound and image, and ZigZag the most varied and adventurous work by the group so far. Robert Smith of The Cure, Johnny Marr and Thom Yorke later named it as an influence.
werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-kaleidosc.listen: Listen to Red Light and notice the rhythmic camera clicks in the minimalist, electronic sound.

werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-the-screa.text:
Siouxsie and the Banshees received a great deal of press attention in 1977, but for a long time could not find a record contract. In June 1978 they signed with Polydor. Many of the songs had already been heard in two radio sessions for John Peel. Steve Lillywhite co-produced. The album was recorded in one week in August 1978 and mixed over three weeks at RAK Studios. Lillywhite had the drums recorded separately: first bass drum and snare, later the cymbals and toms.

The sound is angular and claustrophobic, with sharp guitar, a leading bass and mechanical drums full of toms. There is no real lead instrument: each band member has their own space. The guitars in Suburban Relapse echo the screeching violins from the film music of Psycho. Critics called it a milestone of post-punk. Joy Division and U2 named it as an influence.
werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-the-screa.listen: Listen to Suburban Relapse and notice the guitars that sound like the screeching violins from Psycho. Where do you hear that tension?

werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-tinderbox.text:
Tinderbox came out on 21 April 1986 and is the seventh album by Siouxsie and the Banshees. It was the first full record with guitarist John Valentine Carruthers. The first recordings took place in May 1985 at Hansa by the Wall in Berlin. The band had rehearsed the songs for months, because the album was meant to be played live in its entirety. Cities in Dust and Candyman were released as singles.

The lyrics deal with, among other things, natural disasters and panic. The cover shows a photograph of a tornado from 1927, which had previously appeared on records by Miles Davis and Deep Purple. The song 92 Degrees begins with a clip from the film It Came from Outer Space about murders in high temperatures. Reviewers praised the sharp, full guitars and the vocals. The album reached number 13 in the United Kingdom.
werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-tinderbox.listen: Listen to 92 Degrees and notice the film clip the song begins with. What does that voice say about heat?

werk/sister-rosetta-tharpe-gospel-train.text:
Sister Rosetta Tharpe recorded Gospel Train in July 1956 and released it in December of that year. She was already one of the most successful pioneers of gospel and one of the first to blend gospel with rhythm and blues. Here she is accompanied by musicians from the New York jazz scene, and on several songs the gospel quartet the Harmonizing Four sing along.

The music is firmly rooted in traditional Black gospel, with the occasional touch of blues. The record shows a change of style and points ahead to her influence on blues and blues rock in the 1960s. A reviewer in 2023 heard powerful singing and a fine guitar solo in Can't No Grave Hold Me Down. The album is regarded as a high point in her work. AllMusic called it a super collection, and Tom Moon included it in 1,000 Recordings to Hear Before You Die.
werk/sister-rosetta-tharpe-gospel-train.listen: Listen to Cain't No Grave Hold My Body Down and notice the powerful singing and the short, spirited guitar solo.

werk/skik-op-fietse.text: In 1997 Op fietse by Skik was released, the band of Daniël Lohues from Drenthe, sung in the Drenthe dialect. The song describes a bike ride through the south-east of Drenthe, where Lohues grew up. Lohues sang about ordinary country life, without exaggeration. After Normaal and Rowwen Hèze, Skik showed that even a gentle song in dialect could be played all over the Netherlands.
werk/skik-op-fietse.listen: Hear the relaxed guitar pop and the Drenthe dialect, like a bike ride on a summer's day.

werk/slade-old-new-borrowed-and-blue.text:
In July 1973 drummer Don Powell was seriously injured in a car accident, in which his girlfriend was killed. The band's existence was briefly at stake. Powell recovered and the group went into the studio to record their fourth album, under Chas Chandler. During the recording of My Friend Stan, Powell was still walking with a stick and had to be lifted onto his stool. Around Christmas 1973 Slade also had a number one with Merry Xmas Everybody.

On this album the band tried to break free of the usual rock formula. My Friend Stan and Everyday are songs with piano, and Find Yourself a Rainbow has a pub piano. When the Lights Are Out is the first song on which Jim Lea sings. Alongside softer songs there are also hard-driving rock numbers, such as We're Really Gonna Raise the Roof. The album was released in February 1974 and reached number one in Britain.
werk/slade-old-new-borrowed-and-blue.listen: Listen to Everyday and notice the piano that carries the song, instead of the usual heavy guitars. Compare that with We're Really Gonna Raise the Roof, which sounds more like the Slade you know.

werk/slade-slade-in-flame.text:
Slade in Flame was released on 29 November 1974, the fifth studio album and the first soundtrack album by the British group. Chas Chandler produced it. The band was by now big, but did not want a repeat of the same thing. So they starred in a film about the rise and fall of a fictional 1960s band, Flame. Noddy Holder and Jim Lea wrote the songs and gave them a sixties feel. After an American tour, the band spent a month on the recording.

Far Far Away became a hit, but the ballad How Does It Feel sounded very different from the pop music of the day. The album sold less than the three predecessors, all of which had been number one, and the gloominess of the film confused many fans. Critics were more positive: Classic Rock later placed it at number 18 among the best soundtrack albums.
werk/slade-slade-in-flame.listen: Listen to Standin' On the Corner and notice the brass, which the band used for the first time there, and the swing.

werk/slade-slayed.text:
After their breakthrough with Get Down and Get with It in 1971, Slade scored one hit after another. The live album Slade Alive! reached second place on the album chart in 1972. Slayed? was the third studio album and was released in December 1972, under producer Chas Chandler. Mama Weer All Crazee Now came out as the first single in August and went to number one. The idea for that title came from a doorman in Lincolnshire, who told of a band that had played drunk. Gudbuy T'Jane followed in December and reached number two.

The album sounds stomping and hard, with fat guitar riffs and the screaming vocals of Noddy Holder. Yet there is melancholy in it too, especially in Look at Last Nite, a ballad about fame. Reviewers of the time praised the raw energy. The album topped the British chart and is later counted among the albums you must hear.
werk/slade-slayed.listen: Listen to Mama Weer All Crazee Now and notice the stomping rhythm and Noddy Holder's screaming vocals. Then put Look at Last Nite next to it, to hear how different the same band can sound.

werk/sleater-kinney-all-hands-on-the-bad.text:
All Hands on the Bad One is the fifth album by Sleater-Kinney, released on 2 May 2000 on Kill Rock Stars. After the sombre The Hot Rock, the band did not want to fuss over the sound. According to Corin Tucker, the songs came about spontaneously, one by one. John Goodmanson, who had also produced Dig Me Out, recorded it because he could capture the live sound well. Drummer Janet Weiss sang along for the first time.

The music ranges from soft melodies to fast punk guitars. The lyrics deal with women in rock, morality, eating disorders, feminism and music journalism. The Ballad of a Ladyman mocks how people see women in a band. The reviews were very positive: critics praised the consistency and Tucker's vocals, and the album appeared on end-of-year lists.
werk/sleater-kinney-all-hands-on-the-bad.listen: Listen to Youth Decay and notice the fast guitars beneath the vocals: where does the song sound sharpest?

werk/sleater-kinney-call-the-doctor.text:
Call the Doctor was written in three weeks and recorded in four days, under producer John Goodmanson. It was released on 25 March 1996 on Chainsaw Records. Singer Corin Tucker drew inspiration from a bad job and from the way people in society are turned into products. There is no bassist: the band started with two guitars and liked the fact that the lines could move back and forth between them. Because Tucker and Carrie Brownstein had left their previous bands, the album is sometimes seen as the true debut. Drummer Lora Macfarlane had to leave shortly after the release, because her visa ran out.

The album received a great deal of praise. Robert Christgau lauded the raw energy and Tucker's huge voice. AllMusic called it pure punk. Spin wrote that the band tells stories of everyday struggle instead of the usual female rock tricks. In 2010 Rolling Stone placed it at number 49 among the best albums of the 1990s.
werk/sleater-kinney-call-the-doctor.listen: Listen to the title song Call the Doctor and notice how two guitars and no bass fill the sound, while Tucker's voice leads everything.

werk/sleater-kinney-dig-me-out.text:
Dig Me Out is the third album by Sleater-Kinney, released in 1997 by Kill Rock Stars. It followed the acclaimed Call the Doctor. After that album, drummer Janet Weiss, of Quasi, joined the band. She remained the group's longest-serving drummer. Producer John Goodmanson recorded the album in December 1996 and January 1997 in Seattle. The title refers to the snowstorm that forced the band to literally dig themselves out of the studio.

The record is rawer and rockier than the previous one. The two singers, Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein, take turns and interrupt each other, and without a bassist the guitars can sound huge. One More Hour is about the end of their relationship. The lyrics deal with heartbreak, survival and irritation at sexism. The reviews were glowing, and in retrospect the album is regarded as the band's breakthrough.
werk/sleater-kinney-dig-me-out.listen: Listen to One More Hour. Notice how the voices of Tucker and Brownstein circle around each other and complement each other.

werk/sleater-kinney-sleater-kinney.text:
The self-titled debut of the American band was released on 25 June 1995 on Chainsaw Records, an independent queercore label. The recordings were made by Nick Carrol in Melbourne in Australia, where drummer Lora Macfarlane came from. The producers were Tim Green and the band themselves, at the Red House in Olympia, Washington. Singer and guitarist Corin Tucker said that a thousand copies had been sold by March 1996. Only years later, in 2015, did Nielsen SoundScan put the figure for America at 25,000.

AllMusic described the music as a lo-fi blast of wired riot grrrl rock. Some songs, such as Be Yr Mama, are reminiscent of Sonic Youth, others, such as A Real Man, are pure punk rage. The reviewer found the melodic lines too monotonous, but praised the self-confidence and sense of dynamics, which promised much. Robert Christgau was more positive: in his view the songs about relationships between women revealed deep feelings, which could pass for passion. The reviews were favourable.
werk/sleater-kinney-sleater-kinney.listen: Listen to A Real Man and notice the raw punk energy and the self-confidence with which the band plays its riffs.

werk/sleater-kinney-the-hot-rock.text:
The Hot Rock is the fourth album by Sleater-Kinney and came out on 23 February 1999 on Kill Rock Stars. Major labels offered contracts after Dig Me Out, but the band stayed with the small label. For the first time they worked not with John Goodmanson but with producer Roger Moutenot, in July 1998 in Seattle. They had spent a year writing the songs.

The sound became calmer and gloomier than the raw punk of the earlier records, and the lyrics deal with failed relationships and insecurity. Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein interweave their voices and guitars, for example in The End of You and Burn, Don't Freeze. Get Up was released as a single. The reviews were positive, and it was the first album by the band to reach the American charts.
werk/sleater-kinney-the-hot-rock.listen: Listen to The End of You and notice how the two voices and the guitars circle around each other: who leads when?

werk/slowdive-souvlaki.text:
Souvlaki came about after the relationship between the singers and guitarists Rachel Goswell and Neil Halstead had ended. Halstead increasingly wrote alone. In 1992 the band, touring, was already working on some forty possible songs, but label boss Alan McGee rejected them. Brian Eno refused to produce the album, but did record for a few days with the group, which yielded Sing and Here She Comes. In the summer Halstead withdrew to a rented cottage in Wales and wrote more personal songs there, such as Dagger. Ed Buller mixed the record.

The album was released in June 1993 on Creation Records and received a cool reception, at a time when the press had more eye for Britpop than for shoegaze. Later critics praise it as a classic of the genre, and Pitchfork made a documentary about it in 2015. Halstead names Aphex Twin, dub music and early drum and bass as influences on Souvlaki Space Station.
werk/slowdive-souvlaki.listen: Listen to Sing, one of the songs from the sessions with Brian Eno, and notice how the heavily echoing guitars form a floating whole.

werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-a-whole-ne.text:
In 1967 the debut of Sly and the Family Stone was released, by Epic and CBS. The album was recorded live in the studio, without overdubs, and sounds less poppy than the later records. The lead vocals were shared by Sly Stone, Freddie Stone and Larry Graham. Sly wrote, arranged and produced all the songs himself.

The record received a mixed reception and made no commercial impression: it did not reach the charts. CBS label boss Clive Davis subsequently urged Sly to make a more commercial album. That became Dance to the Music. This made A Whole New Thing a kind of run-up: here the band is still raw and idiosyncratic, before the sound was smoothed out for a bigger audience.
werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-a-whole-ne.listen: Listen to Underdog and notice the loose, direct playing of a band that is playing live in the studio.

werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-dance-to-t.text:
The second album by Sly and the Family Stone was released in April 1968. It exists because CBS executive Clive Davis wanted Sly Stone to make his sound more accessible. The band itself did not think much of it during the recording. Sly came up with a formula: the lead singers, Sly, Freddie Stone, Larry Graham and the new Rose Stone, share the vocals, by singing in chorus or alternating line by line. Through it all, his message of peace, brotherly love and opposition to racism remained intact.

The formula worked. The title song became a top ten hit and was regarded as influential on psychedelic soul and as a preparation for funk. Other soul groups began to adopt this sound, the Temptations already at the end of 1968. Later The Jackson 5 and Undisputed Truth also took on influences. The album closes its first side with the Dance to the Medley.
werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-dance-to-t.listen: Listen to Dance to the Music and notice how the singers alternate within the same lines.

werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-life.text:
Life is the third studio album by Sly and the Family Stone and was released in September 1968 on Epic. In the United Kingdom it was called M'Lady. Unlike its predecessor Dance to the Music, it was not a commercial success, although the reviews have been mostly positive over the years. The album is a halfway point between the fiery A Whole New Thing and the more commercial Dance to the Music and uses few studio effects.

The music comes mainly from Sly Stone's compositions. The songs are about dating, about groupies and about phoneys, as in Plastic Jim, which refers to Eleanor Rigby. Fun, Harmony, Life and Love City revolve around unity and integration, themes that Stand! would later develop. Much of the material has been sampled: Greg Errico's drum solo in Love City, and the opening riff of Into My Own Thing in Weapon of Choice by Fatboy Slim.
werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-life.listen: Listen to Love City and notice the drum solo by Greg Errico, which has often been sampled since.

werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-stand.text:
Stand! is the fourth album by Sly and the Family Stone and came out on 3 May 1969 on Epic Records, shortly before the Woodstock performance. Sly Stone wrote and produced it himself. It followed Life, which had not worked commercially: none of the first three albums had got above position 100 on the Billboard chart. A large part was recorded at Pacific High Recording Studios in San Francisco. Stephen Paley remembered how concentrated Sly was at the time.

The record contains Stand!, I Want to Take You Higher, Sing a Simple Song and Everyday People, already a number 1 when the album came out. In Everyday People, Larry Graham introduces the slap-pop bass. Sex Machine is a thirteen-minute jam in which every band member gets a solo. The album reached number 13 and became one of the most successful of the 1960s. It mixes rock, funk and soul, and white and Black voices.
werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-stand.listen: Listen to I Want to Take You Higher and notice how the singers take turns on the lead vocal. Can you hear all seven band members shouting along in the background?

werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-there-s-a-.text:
After the success of Stand! and the Woodstock performance, Sly Stone did not deliver a new album for a long time. Meanwhile his drug use increased, tensions in the band grew and drummer Gregg Errico left in early 1971. Stone recorded most of it himself, in Sausalito and in his home studio in Bel Air, often alone, with overdubs and a primitive little drum machine.

The result sounds much darker than the cheerful records before it: sharp funk rhythms, a dense mix and lyrics full of apathy and disappointment about the sixties and about his own fame. The title was at first Africa Talks to You, but was changed in response to What's Going On by Marvin Gaye. Family Affair became a number one. The first reviews were mixed, but the album is now regarded as one of the most influential records ever, especially for funk, jazz-funk and hip hop.
werk/sly-and-the-family-stone-there-s-a-.listen: Listen to Family Affair and notice the shuffling drum machine rhythm and the languid, almost resigned vocals.

werk/small-faces-ogdens-nut-gone-flake.text:
Ogdens' Nut Gone Flake was released on 24 May 1968 and was the third album by Small Faces, their only concept album. It spent six weeks at number 1 in England. The recording took about five months, mainly at Olympic Studios in Barnes. The title and packaging parodied a brand of tobacco in a tin, and the first edition came in a round metal tin which soon proved too expensive.

The first side shows all kinds of styles, from Cockney singalongs such as Lazy Sunday to the soul ballad Afterglow. The second side tells a fairy tale about Happiness Stan, who searches for the missing half of the moon. Comedian Stanley Unwin links the six songs with his nonsense language Unwinese. The idea arose during a boat trip on the Thames after a failed tour of Australia and New Zealand. Because of its complexity, the band never played the album live in its entirety.
werk/small-faces-ogdens-nut-gone-flake.listen: Listen to Happiness Stan and notice the voice of Stanley Unwin between the songs. Can you hear his invented language as a narrator in a fairy tale?

werk/smokey-robinson-a-quiet-storm.text:
A Quiet Storm was released in March 1975 as Smokey Robinson's third solo album. He had left his group the Miracles and, after two disappointing records, his solo career needed a new impetus. He wrote and arranged all the songs himself, except for two that he wrote with a co-writer. Guitarist Marv Tarplin of the Miracles contributed, as did bassist James Jamerson.

The album sounds calm and romantic. The long title track Quiet Storm lasts almost eight minutes, and Baby That's Backatcha became the hit and took it to number 1 on the Billboard Hot Soul Singles for a week. It was also his first disco hit. Critics reacted mostly positively. Robert Palmer praised his singing and production in Rolling Stone. The album is regarded as an example of what later came to be called the quiet storm radio format, and Q counted it among the best Motown albums in 1999.
werk/smokey-robinson-a-quiet-storm.listen: Listen to Quiet Storm and notice how slowly the song builds: what kind of mood do the soft accompaniment and the vocals create together, and does that mood stay the same for all eight minutes?

werk/smokey-robinson-deep-in-my-soul.text:
Deep in My Soul was released in 1977 and was Smokey Robinson's fifth solo album. Berry Gordy was executive producer. The album contains eight songs, almost all by other writers. That was new for a singer who had built his fame on his own songs for the Miracles.

According to the source, various Motown writers try here to approximate the clear, direct style of the younger Robinson. According to the reviewer Robert Christgau, they succeed on four songs, two of which open each side of the record. Robinson then sings them as if he had written them himself. The Los Angeles Times found his singing excellent, but also felt that he needed strong melodies of his own to recapture the sheen of the Miracles. The album thus shows how dependent Robinson was on good material.
werk/smokey-robinson-deep-in-my-soul.listen: Listen to Vitamin U, the opening track, and notice how Robinson makes his vocals sound: does this sound like a song he might have written himself?

werk/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles-awa.text:
Away We a Go-Go from 1966 is an album by Smokey Robinson & The Miracles. It contains two singles: (Come 'Round Here) I'm the One You Need, written and produced by Holland-Dozier-Holland and a hit in the Billboard top 20, and Whole Lot of Shakin' in My Heart (Since I Met You) by Frank Wilson. The album contains a different take of I'm the One You Need than the single.

A large part consists of covers of recent hits: You Don't Have to Say You Love Me by Dusty Springfield, two songs by Dionne Warwick, Walk On By and I Just Don't Know What to Do with Myself, and Beauty Is Only Skin Deep by The Temptations, which the group had already recorded in 1964. Baby Baby is an original song by the Lewis Sisters. Claudette Robinson does not appear on the front of the sleeve but does on the back.
werk/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles-awa.listen: Listen to Baby Baby, an original song by the Lewis Sisters, and notice the vocals of Smokey Robinson.

werk/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles-mak.text:
Make It Happen from 1967 is an album by Smokey Robinson & The Miracles. It contains ballads such as the hits The Love I Saw in You Was Just a Mirage and More Love, and the swinging The Tears of a Clown, which was written with Stevie Wonder and his producer Hank Cosby. Wonder also co-wrote After You Put Back the Pieces and My Love Is Your Love (Forever). Holland-Dozier-Holland supplied the danceable It's a Good Feeling.

Three years after the album appeared, The Tears of a Clown was released as a single and reached number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the British chart. For that reason the album was reissued under that title in 1970. AllMusic gave it four and a half stars and called it the group's most underrated album of the 1960s.
werk/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles-mak.listen: Listen to The Tears of a Clown and notice the contrast between the cheerful music and the title.

werk/smokey-robinson-pure-smokey.text:
Pure Smokey is Smokey Robinson's second studio album and was released on 15 March 1974 on Tamla Records. It is one of the first records he made after leaving the Miracles. Guitarist Marv Tarplin, who left the group a year after Robinson, followed him to California to help him with his solo work. Together they wrote several songs for this album.

Robinson produced almost everything himself, only A Tattoo he made together with Willie Hutch. The arrangements were by Russ Turner, Gene Page and Robinson himself. Among those playing on the record are Bobbye Hall on percussion, Henry Davis on bass guitar and Jeffrey Osborne on drums. Virgin Man was released as a single, at five minutes the longest song on the record.
werk/smokey-robinson-pure-smokey.listen: Listen to Virgin Man, the single from the album, and notice how Robinson's voice carries the song above the band.

werk/snelle-smoorverliefd.text: In 2020 Snelle from Deventer had a number 1 hit with Smoorverliefd, a love song that went with a campaign against phone use while cycling. Snelle began as a rapper and increasingly turned to singing. He released his first records on his own label. Anyone who wanted to get on the radio in the past had to go through record bosses and DJs. A new generation also found its audience through streaming and social media.
werk/snelle-smoorverliefd.listen: Hear the simple guitar and the rap that turns into singing. A rapper who makes pop songs.

werk/soft-cell-non-stop-erotic-cabaret.text:
Soft Cell's debut album was released on 27 November 1981 on Some Bizzare Records. It was made on a small budget. Producer Mike Thorne lent out his Synclavier, an instrument that was normally far beyond the duo's reach. The title comes from a real sign outside a strip club in Soho.

The album was carried by the single Tainted Love, a cover of Gloria Jones that topped the charts worldwide. Bedsitter and Say Hello, Wave Goodbye also made the top five in England. Marc Almond later said that the record tells the story of a man with a dull suburban life who seeks out the wild life in Soho. He has an affair, but returns to his wife. Neil Tennant called it a musical. Sex Dwarf caused an uproar, as its video was banned for its S&M imagery. Reviews were mostly positive. Melody Maker spoke of a brilliant indictment of the emptiness of pop, while NME found the concept hollow.
werk/soft-cell-non-stop-erotic-cabaret.listen: Listen to Sex Dwarf and notice how the electronic music and the vocals together create a dark, theatrical atmosphere, as in a cabaret.

werk/soft-machine-fourth.text:
Fourth was released in 1971, the fourth album by Soft Machine. The cover shows only the numeral 4. It is the first album that is entirely instrumental. On the previous album, Third, the band had already moved from its psychedelic and progressive early years towards instrumental jazz. Elton Dean plays alto saxophone and saxello, Mike Ratledge acoustic piano, electric piano and organ, Hugh Hopper bass and fuzz bass, and Robert Wyatt drums.

As on its predecessor, a few tracks receive help from additional musicians: Mark Charig on cornet, Nick Evans on trombone, Roy Babbington on double bass and others on saxophone, flute and bass clarinet. Hopper wrote most of the compositions. It was the last album with Wyatt, one of the founders. He had already made a solo album, The End of an Ear, and then started the group Matching Mole, a pun on the French Machine Molle, soft machine.
werk/soft-machine-fourth.listen: Listen to Virtually, Pt. 1 and notice how bass, piano and brass together form one long, instrumental composition without vocals.

werk/soft-machine-seven.text:
Seven is the seventh studio album by Soft Machine and came out in 1973. Bassist Roy Babbington, who had already played as a session musician on Fourth and Fifth, became a permanent member. He replaced Hugh Hopper, who began a solo career. As a result, more than half of the band now consisted of former members of Nucleus. The line-up also included Karl Jenkins, Mike Ratledge and drummer John Marshall.

The album was released on CBS in the United Kingdom, with a colourful gatefold sleeve, and on Columbia in the United States. The sleeve there shows the numeral 7. The titles of the last two tracks, The German Lesson and The French Lesson, were clearly intended as a joke by the band. It was the last studio album with a number as its title.
werk/soft-machine-seven.listen: Listen to Down the Road and notice how the song ends in a floating jumble of keyboards.

werk/solomon-burke-rock-n-soul.text:
Rock 'n Soul is a studio album by Solomon Burke from 1964, released on Atlantic Records. The title refers to the nickname King of Rock 'n' Soul, which he liked to bear. According to him, there was no rock without soul and no soul without rock. The rhythm and blues label went against him, because he led a clean life and was deeply religious. His coronation as king at the Royal Theatre in Baltimore was reported in Jet in January 1964.

The album features seven hits from the Billboard Top 100, including Just Out of Reach, Cry to Me, Can't Nobody Love You, If You Need Me and Goodbye Baby (Baby Goodbye). The New Rolling Stone Album Guide called his version of He'll Have to Go a heart-rending interpretation. Cry to Me has, according to AllMusic, a light Caribbean rhythm at a cheerful tempo, while the lyrics are in fact solemn. The record appears in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
werk/solomon-burke-rock-n-soul.listen: Listen to Cry to Me and notice the contrast between the cheerful, lightly Caribbean rhythm and the solemn lyrics.

werk/sonny-rollins-saxophone-colossus.text:
On 22 June 1956 Sonny Rollins recorded this album in Rudy Van Gelder's studio in Hackensack, New Jersey, for Prestige Records. The producer was Bob Weinstock. It was his sixth studio album. The saxophonist led a quartet with pianist Tommy Flanagan, bassist Doug Watkins and drummer Max Roach. At the time he was also playing in the quintet of Clifford Brown and Roach. The recording took place four days before Brown and Richie Powell were killed in a car accident on the way to a gig in Chicago.

The record was regarded as a breakthrough and made the saxophonist known as a jazz musician of stature. Billboard wrote in 1957 that every track was full of surprises and that every solo was built with great architectural logic. DownBeat praised the humour and the gentleness, combined with undiminished, powerful swing. The Penguin Guide to Jazz included the album in its core selection. In 2016 it was preserved in the Library of Congress's National Recording Registry.
werk/sonny-rollins-saxophone-colossus.listen: Listen to how, on Blue 7, the saxophonist builds his solo step by step, with each new idea growing out of the last.

werk/sonny-rollins-the-sound-of-sonny.text:
The Sound of Sonny was released in 1957 and was the first album Sonny Rollins recorded for the Riverside label. That year he began working for several labels, which at the time was almost considered sacrilege. Playing with him were pianist Sonny Clark, drummer Roy Haynes and bassist Percy Heath or Paul Chambers. Orrin Keepnews was the producer.

According to the AllMusic reviewer Lindsay Planer, a new phase began in the saxophonist's career in 1957. He was playing at his best: Down Beat declared him New Star among tenor saxophonists in the critics' poll. On the record you hear, according to Planer, the fluent solos and new melodic high points, and a new freedom, including in the line-up. The bassist changes from track to track, and on a few tracks the piano or the drums do not play.
werk/sonny-rollins-the-sound-of-sonny.listen: Listen to the fluent tenor saxophone solo on Just in Time and how it develops above the rhythm section.

werk/sonny-rollins-way-out-west.text:
Way Out West was recorded in Los Angeles in 1957, the first time on the West Coast for Sonny Rollins, a New Yorker. He played with bassist Ray Brown and drummer Shelly Manne, with whom he had never played before. It was his first album with only bass and drums, without a pianist or guitarist playing chords. According to producer Lester Koenig, the recording began at three o'clock in the morning, because the schedules were full. At seven o'clock, after four hours of concentrated work and with half of the album on tape, the saxophonist said that only now was he really getting into his stride.

The title has several meanings. The record was made in the West, with musicians from West Coast jazz, and contains songs from country music, such as I'm an Old Cowhand and Wagon Wheels. On the cover he stands in a cowboy hat with a holster, an idea of his own, photographed by William Claxton. AllMusic calls it one of his high points.
werk/sonny-rollins-way-out-west.listen: Listen to I'm an Old Cowhand to hear how saxophone, bass and drums together make a full sound without a piano or guitar playing chords.

werk/sonny-rollins-work-time.text:
Work Time dates from 1956 and was released on the Prestige label. Sonny Rollins plays tenor saxophone in a quartet with pianist Ray Bryant, bassist George Morrow and drummer Max Roach. The record contains five tracks: standards by Irving Berlin and Cole Porter, the piece Raincheck by Billy Strayhorn and Paradox, an original composition by Rollins.

Opinions differ on its reception. Scott Yanow of AllMusic found it a pleasant, strong album that is not essential. The writer and musician Peter Niklas Wilson, by contrast, called it one of Rollins's most brilliant sessions and put it on a par with the recordings of Saxophone Colossus, which so many fans love.
werk/sonny-rollins-work-time.listen: Listen to There's No Business Like Show Business to hear how the tenor saxophone handles the familiar melody and how drummer Max Roach moves along underneath it.

werk/sons-of-kemet-black-to-the-future.text:
Black to the Future is the fourth and last studio album by the British jazz group Sons of Kemet. It was released on 14 May 2021 on Impulse! Records. The core of the group consisted of Shabaka Hutchings on tenor saxophone and wind instruments, Theon Cross on tuba and the drummers Tom Skinner and Edward Wakili-Hick. In addition, Steve Williamson played tenor saxophone.

On the record many guests sing and speak, among them Joshua Idehen, Angel Bat Dawid, Moor Mother, D Double E, Kojey Radical and Lianne La Havas. A number of them are credited as guests alongside the track titles. Critics received the album very positively.
werk/sons-of-kemet-black-to-the-future.listen: Listen to Field Negus to hear how Joshua Idehen's voice relates to the group's wind instruments and drummers.
